findings.evidence: candidate.diff, template/scripts/agent_friction.py hunk @@ -1411: `main = read_platform_config(root)["main_branch"]` sits inside `try: ... except Exception: main = "main"`. A missing file or key is therefore silently replaced by "main". The spec says scripts SHALL NOT supply per-call-site defaults for required keys.
findings.summary: agent_friction.changed_paths still swallows every configuration failure and substitutes a default main branch. The change removed this same pattern from non_task_names, so the fallback is now inconsistent.

findings.evidence: candidate.diff, template/scripts/capability_manager.py: `config = _load_toml(root / ".dev-platform.toml")` followed by `raw = config["agent_tools"]`. The reader is not used and the one-line diagnostic hook does not apply to a KeyError.
findings.summary: capability_manager.configured_providers still loads .dev-platform.toml through its own raw loader. It now indexes `config["agent_tools"]` directly, so a missing key raises a bare KeyError instead of the named PlatformConfigError. The other raw loaders (dev.py, platform_bootstrap, shared_workspace, requirement_integration) were routed through the validated reader.

findings.evidence: candidate.diff, template/scripts/shared_workspace.py hunk @@ -104: the old `if not config_path.is_file(): return False` is replaced by `return _configured(integration)["workflow_profile"] == "multi-agent"`, inside the unchanged `except (OSError, SharedWorkspaceError)`. PlatformConfigError subclasses RuntimeError.
findings.summary: shared_workspace_applicable now calls the validating reader. Its except clause covers only (OSError, SharedWorkspaceError), so a missing or invalid config now propagates PlatformConfigError out of what was a boolean predicate. Previously it returned False for a missing file. The new behavior may be intended, but it is not called out in the design.
